(2) Delete-the-gate was performed literally, twice (once per function), using a new DB-less spy suite: commenting out each function's `if (!canRunStudioReport(entitlement))` check made that function's own spy test go RED (and only that one -- the other stayed green, ruling out a suite-wide false positive) with the exact expected failure mode (the code reached the throwing fake db instead of refusing pre-query); both mutations were reverted before commit, confirmed via `git diff` showing zero residue. canRunStudioReport(snap) is a pure synchronous predicate over an already-resolved SmartsiteEntitlementSnapshot (requireAuthContext reads AsyncLocalStorage populated once per request). 'Build the test at the level where the entitlement is resolved', a falsifier's own fallback instruction for when a live sub-tier account is unavailable, is therefore both possible and cheap here -- no mock server, no live account, no DB needed to prove the gate's decision logic; only the LIVE WIRING from a real HTTP request to that snapshot remains genuinely unverifiable without a live sub-Studio account.

A DB-less spy (a fake `db` object whose `select()` throws if called) is a stronger, faster, and more direct non-vacuousness proof for an early-return gate than asserting the response SHAPE alone: it proves the gate runs BEFORE any query is even built, and it lets falsifier-2-style delete-the-gate mutation testing run in milliseconds with zero Postgres dependency, reserving the real integration DB only for the positive/data-shape tests that actually need it.

drizzle-orm's postgres-js error wrapping puts the full query text AND every selected column name into the thrown error's own .message (not just a generic 'invalid input syntax' string) -- live-confirmed against production, and worse than what the row's own quoted excerpt implied (14 column names, not just the table name). A raw-error audit on any drizzle-backed route should assume the WHOLE select list is exposed, not just the table.
